text:
alex: quick ask — can someone run a focused micro-benchmark comparing API overhead for streaming vs non-streaming when we trigger function/tool calls and when we return structured JSON output? need p50/p95 lat, token throughput, CPU/GPU % and rough per-token cost. short/med/long payloads.

maria: I can do it. which model and branch? any specific harness you want me to use?

alex: thanks. use model: redwood/llama-13b-quant-v2. branch: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/feature/api-overhead-2026. script: 
```bash
./run_overhead.sh \
  --model redwood/llama-13b-quant-v2 \
  --modes non-streaming,streaming \
  --features "function_calling,structured_output" \
  --prompts ./prompt_sets/{short,medium,long}.json \
  --warmup 50 \
  --iters 200 \
  --csv out/overhead_results.csv
```

alex: measure both client-observed end-to-end and server-side decode time (we have server timestamps in logs). include per-request token count column. prefer CSV + a 1-paragraph summary. ping me @maria when done. :pray:

maria: got it. I'll run on dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (A100s) and also a single-host dev box (rt-dev-01) to show infra differences. ETA 2h.

ops-bot: scheduled job "overhead-benchmark-171066" queued on dedicated-gpu-pool-3 by maria. estimated runtime ~45m.

maria: quick question — for structured_output case, should I test both strict JSON schema enforcement (response must validate) and best-effort JSON?

alex: yes — include both. label columns schema_strict / schema_relaxed. for function_calling, test sync function call (single callback) and streaming callbacks (tool emits chunks).

maria: starting run now. I'll paste partial CSV when first results come in.

bench-bot: overhead-benchmark-171066 completed on dedicated-gpu-pool-3. results uploaded to s3://redwood-benchmarks/171066/overhead_results.csv

maria: partial summary (dedicated pool):
```
mode,feature,prompt,size_tokens,p50_ms,p95_ms,throughput_tok_s,cpu_pct,gpu_pct,per_token_cost_us,notes
non-streaming,none,short,22,85,120,420,18,32,0.015,baseline
streaming,none,short,22,70,110,540,20,35,0.018,slightly faster client latency
non-streaming,function_calling,short,30,130,220,320,22,40,0.020,extra overhead for invocation/serialization
streaming,function_calling,short,30,95,160,430,25,45,0.024,streamed callbacks reduce tail
non-streaming,structured_schema_strict,short,26,150,260,300,21,38,0.021,validation cost
streaming,structured_schema_strict,short,26,110,180,410,24,43,0.025,stream + schema validation helps p50
```

maria: notable: streaming reduces client-observed p50 by ~15-30% for short prompts, and function_calling adds a consistent ~30-50ms overhead non-streamed. schema_strict validation adds CPU load and raises per-token cost ~10-20%.

tim: thanks — can you also share server_decode_time vs network_wait_time? curious if p95 is network dominated.

maria: yes. for p95 of long prompts network wait ~40% on dedicated pool (client chunking), server_decode_time still majority for long sequences. i'll include separate columns server_decode_ms and network_ms in final CSV.

jin: for the dev-box runs, did you see any quantization-performance regressions vs prod pool?

maria: dev-box (rt-dev-01) had higher variance and ~20% slower throughput for long sequences, likely due to CPU combiner and smaller NVLink config. no correctness regressions.

alex: awesome — can you open a short RFC-ish PR with the CSV + 1-paragraph conclusions and recommended defaults (e.g., default: streaming for short interactive flows; function calling: prefer streaming callbacks; schema_strict only when required)? tag me and eng-ml.

maria: will do. PR coming in ~30m (bench: #815).

alex: perfect. once PR is in we'll schedule a 15-min sync to decide console defaults.

tim: heads-up: if we set streaming default we should update SDK docs and call out per-token cost differences. I'll add a docs todo.

maria: uploaded final CSV + server breakdown: s3://redwood-benchmarks/171066/overhead_results-final.csv. PR #815 created with link.

alex: thanks all — big help. can we mark this resolved after the docs + console flag review? :white_check_mark:
